recipes.name: Steve's Bourbon Buffalo Wing Sauce
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon hot sauce (such as Frank's RedHot ®)

steps.text: Stir the bourbon, brown sugar, ketchup, white vinegar, hot sauce, cayenne pepper, garlic powder, honey, and butter together in a saucepan over medium heat; cook, whisking occasionally, until the mixture begins to bubble. Reduce heat to low and cook at a gentle simmer, whisking occasionally, until the sauce thickens nearly to the consistency of maple syrup or molasses, about 15 minutes. Remove from heat and allow to cool.

raw_recipe.headline: Steve's Bourbon Buffalo Wing Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Try this sticky, Bourbon-spiked alternative to buttery hot sauce for your next batch of chicken wings.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is amazing. For best results make sure to use bourbon since it is important for the flavor and let the sauce sit in the fridge for a day or so. Adding 1-2 tsp of Tabasco sauce will also add some more heat if you're looking for something more spicy.

This is a 5 star sauce with a modifcation. For the people who say it was too sweet and want more heat... I used "reduced sugar" ketchup, left out the 1/4 of brown sugar and just used the 1 Tablespoon of honey. Then used Tobasco Habenero sauce and doubled the cayenne. Less sweet with twice the heat. Perfect. (Optional.. take the pan and smoke the sauce with hickory wood in your grill or smoker.)

Wow, this sauce was amazing.
I smoked the wings and tossed them in this prior to serving.
AMAZING
I didn't have honey so i substituted Agave Nector
I didn't have Franks so i substituted Valentina
Everyone that had them thought they were delicious.
Thanks for the Recipe!

Hubby has an aversion to hot, so we omitted the cayenne and hot sauce. Poured over sautéed chicken breast cubes and cooked to caramelize it just a bit. Served over white rice. Hubby and adult daughter raved over it with every other bite. Definitely adding to our rotation!

I made this sauce with some small alterations. I added two tables spoons of hot sauce, I also doubled the garlic powder and cayenne and added 1/2 teaspoon of onion powder. This made a delicious and flavorful sauce with no strong bourbon taste but it was still delicious and evident. I will be using this recipe again. KUDOS
This recipe is awesome. Very easy to get creative with as well. I like to sauté some habaneros in the butter , strain them out, and mix it in for a bit more of a kick.

Great sauce and rave reviews from those that have eaten it.

My daughters and I made a version of this for a BBQ competition and took third in the People's choice wing competition. We did make some adjustments- I do a 4x version, but take 1 cup bourbon and boil it to about a teaspoon. I then add that to the regular recipe- adjusting the amounts based on the hot sauce I use until I get sweet/ smoky on the front with a kick of heat on the back end. I think this recipe gives a nice balance of favors as nothing overpowers the others when done right.

I have made this recipe twice now, two weekend Sundays in a row. Absolutely love this recipe. So delicious. Just the right amount of sweet and heat. I have altered it a bit for my own taste. I used less ketchup and more franks. Also, the quality of bourbon you use makes a difference. I used Buffalo Trace bourbon which has that hearty oaky flavor. When you cook it down to cook out the alcohol, you are left with that amazing smoky oaky-ness. Love it!!

I have made this several times now and definitely love it. I didn't have bourbon or honey BUT I had Jack Daniel's Tennessee Honey! let me tell you that worked perfectly! and I was reading between two recipes and added Worcestershire, but that is a great addition to this! only gave four stars because I didn't quite follow the recipe! this is my go-to for wings!

I was totally out of hot sauce, but I had some sriracha. Only needed about 1/2 tbsp for plenty of heat. Otherwise followed exactly. This will now be a staple. So easy, and absolutely delicious! Thanks.

I’ve made these twice. Exactly as written as much as possible. Except the first time I used swerve brown sugar to decrease the carbs and second time with regular brown sugar. I didn’t have the cayenne pepper so I used smoked paprika. Same each time. THE ABSOLUTE BEST wing sauce ever. Tastes just like the ones from a restaurant down the street. I used Jim Beam. For those reviews who say the bourbon flavor is to strong, try cooking it longer. I don’t like straight bourbon and I I didn’t notice. Also not spicy...I don’t like spicy I like to taste the flavor. This is a keeper, I will double it next time and cook a whole bag of wings. Can’t wait to make for company.
awesome
Best wing sauce ever

My only regret when making this sauce was not making more! I love that i can make this as spicy or sweet as I want. I like a little less heat than my family and they like a little less sweet... so I just make 2 batches and adjust as needed. My absolute favorite wing sauce.
This recipe is awesome!!!
Real good! Had to make a few small subs but it was delicious. Will definitely make again.

Sounds delish!!! Can't wait to make em. Ok, I made the sauce last night for air fried chicken wings. Fantastic, delicious, make these again, taste so good, licked the pan clean....only a few superlatives that my husband used. I encourage you to make these. I doubled the recipe to make sure the wings were thoroughly coated. Enough said, just make it. P.S. We ended up buying a cheaper brand of bourbon as he did not allow me to use his expensive bourbon!!!!
Absolutely Awesome!!!

This is hands down the best wing sauce recipe. I make it exactly as written. My husband requests it every time I cook crispy chicken wings. Sometimes I double the recipe just because we love it so much!
Good
